contradictions.explanation: Both claims refer to the same rule for employees’ casual leave but give different entitlements (18 days vs 20 days). The second claim’s condition is a version label, which does not override the first, so the documents conflict.

statement_1.text: Employees are entitled to 18 days of casual leave per year.

statement_2.text: Employees are entitled to 20 days of casual leave per year as per the new circular.

contradictions.explanation: Claim A permits remote work up to 2 days per week with manager approval, while Claim B states remote work is not allowed unless HR gives written approval, so the two rules conflict for the same group of employees.

statement_1.text: Employees may work remotely up to 2 days per week with prior approval from their manager.

statement_2.text: Remote work is not permitted for any employee without written approval from HR.

contradictions.explanation: Both claims address remote work for employees, but Claim A limits all employees to 2 days per week with manager approval, while Claim B grants the marketing team unrestricted remote work without approval, directly conflicting the same rule for a subset of employees.

statement_1.text: Employees may work remotely up to 2 days per week with prior approval from their manager.

statement_2.text: The marketing team is allowed to work remotely without any approval.

contradictions.explanation: The policy says employees cannot work remotely without HR approval, yet it also states the marketing team can work remotely without any approval, which conflicts because the marketing team is a subset of employees.

statement_1.text: Remote work is not permitted for any employee without written approval from HR.

statement_2.text: The marketing team is allowed to work remotely without any approval.
